task: Add structured INFO/WARNING observability logging across the mcp_auth OAuth2 initiate/discovery bridge layer plus a fire-and-forget UI timeout beacon in codemie-ui's useAuthCallbackListener hook.

key_reasoning.reason: 5 backend bridge files (_common.py, _initiate.py, _discovery.py, _oauth2_callback.py, _diagnostics.py) plus 1 frontend hook (useAuthCallbackListener.ts) span 2 layers; base M bumped to L because _common.py is a core shared utility used across ~15 call sites in _initiate.py, _oauth2_callback.py, and _post_auth.py, and the CWE-117 sanitizer may relocate into it.

Base M — established log-line conventions (message prefix, key=value pairs, INFO/WARNING split, CWE-117 sanitizer) already exist verbatim in the same package. Bumped to L by the explicit security requirement: no secrets logged (client_secret, full state, code_verifier, tokens), enforced sanitization, and a dedicated test asserting state redaction (AC7).

9 files touched, all modified, 0 new files: 5 backend bridge files + 2 existing backend test files + 1 frontend hook + 1 existing frontend test file, spanning 3-4 directories (mcp_auth/, tests/enterprise/mcp_auth/, codemie-ui/src/hooks/, codemie-ui/src/hooks/__tests__/).

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from M to L: touches core shared utility _common.py (used across ~15 call sites in 3 files).
Technical Risk bumped from M to L: security/compliance requirement — no-secrets-in-logs constraint (AC7) with CWE-117 sanitizer and a dedicated state-redaction test.

component_scope.label: L
component_scope.reason: Predicted 5 backend files + 1 hook; actual 6 backend source files (router.py was also needed to thread mcp_config_id into the static and SAML builders) + 1 hook, across 2 repos. The _common.py concern proved real: three shared helpers now serve every initiate path, the discovery resolver and the callback.

requirements_clarity.label: S
requirements_clarity.reason: Nine ACs were unambiguous and each mapped to a task. The one genuine open question surfaced only at review (CR-005 - whether the timeout beacon can carry a state prefix) and was resolved by a scoping decision, not rework.

technical_risk.label: XL
technical_risk.reason: Bumped from L. The security requirement bit exactly where predicted but harder: the CWE-117 sanitizer was bypassed by _log_state_prefix on a value the callback receives unauthenticated and logs before verification (AC7 fail), and observing the flow could break it two ways - an unguarded duplicate authorize-URL parse raising after the PKCE write (AC8), and a resolution INFO whose attribute reads sat inside the handler that reports resolution failure. All three were found by code review, not by the implementation's own tests.

file_change_estimate.label: XL
file_change_estimate.reason: Bumped from L. 1372 insertions / 30 deletions across 10 codemie files plus 191 insertions across 2 codemie-ui files. Test code dominates: 944 lines added to test_oauth2_initiate_bridge.py alone. Two pre-existing bridge test files also needed realignment once the branch widened build_saml_initiate_response and started reading resolution.auth_config_id.

dependencies.label: XS
dependencies.reason: Confirmed. codemie-enterprise stayed untouched - the authorize URL and the discovered-flow snapshot already exposed every field needed, exactly as scoped.

affected_layers.label: M
affected_layers.reason: Confirmed: bridge/service layer, REST router, and the frontend hook.

drivers: technical_risk L->XL: the three blocking review findings were all in the observability code's own failure modes - a log line that could forge log lines, a log line that could 500 a successful flow, and a log line whose failure was reported as a business failure.
file_change_estimate L->XL: the test-to-source ratio was far higher than assumed (~10:1 by line count), because every log line needed a caplog assertion per flow path.

Unpredicted: widening two public builder signatures broke pre-existing bridge tests the plan's in-scope file list never named. The quality gates caught it; the review lenses had flagged the risk (CR-016) and an incomplete grep of src/ only had let it through.
lessons: A logging-only ticket is not low-risk when the values logged are attacker-influenced and the code runs on an authentication path.
Plan in-scope file lists should include the files a signature change forces, not only the files carrying the feature.
Moving a log call out of a broad try/except is correct for attribution but transfers the raise risk - it needs its own guard in the same change.
